instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS-lens R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020H.2 at branch feature/wp-scp-022-020h2-regal-sha256, commit 6d248f3. The slice closes the TF-020H3-001 supply-chain gap by adding SHA256 verification to the Regal binary download in policy-check.yml. THINK ADVERSARIALLY about the supply-chain hardening: did the closure actually close the attack surface, or does the implementation have a gap? VERIFY: (1) The verify_sha256 call in resolve_regal() actually runs BEFORE the binary is executed. Trace the order: resolve_regal() returns the path of the verified binary; cp to BIN_DIR/regal; chmod +x; runtime smoke test (`regal version`). Could a TOCTOU attacker swap the file between verify_sha256 and the cp/exec? (Probably not because /tmp/RUNNER_TEMP is the runner's private tmp, but worth confirming.) (2) The vendor fallback path: `vendor/regal/${REGAL_ASSET}`. If an attacker compromises an adopter's repo and adds a malicious binary at vendor/regal/regal_Linux_x86_64 with the matching SHA256 (i.e. the upstream file unmodified), what's the attack? The vendor file itself is benign in that case. But could an attacker push a malicious binary AND simultaneously update the lockfile in the same PR? Yes — but that's the same risk as any code review bypass. CODEOWNERS protection on scripts/scp-policy-check.lock should be the control. Verify CODEOWNERS coverage. (3) The lockfile shape: regal block uses single-binary (no archive). If a future Regal release moves to a tarball-shipping shape, the lockfile + resolve_regal would need both archive_sha256 and binary sha256. Is this future-proof, or will a routine version bump silently break? (4) Sigstore attestation: NOT added here. The DISPATCH-NOTE explicitly defers this to TF-007 (re-tighten when OPA upstream begins publishing). Is this acceptable, or should Regal get an attempt + soft-warn even now? Note: the existing OPA call uses `gh attestation verify` which fails (404) on every run today. Adding a similar attempt for Regal would just add another 404 + soft-warn pair to the log — symmetric noise. The decision to skip is consistent with the Conftest pattern. (5) The `chmod +x` happens after cp from RUNNER_TEMP. If RUNNER_TEMP is somehow group-writable, an attacker on the runner host could swap the binary between cp and chmod. Verify RUNNER_TEMP permissions on ubuntu-24.04 — should be 0700 owned by runner user. (6) read_tool_version awk filter: an adopter's tool-versions file with malformed content (e.g., 'regal 0.40.0; rm -rf /' as the version) — does awk preserve the malicious chars in the printed value, and would they then propagate into REGAL_VERSION and into the URL path? Trace: REGAL_REPO="https://github.com/open-policy-agent/regal/releases/download/v${REGAL_VERSION}" — the v${} concat is shell-context, so a semicolon would be a URL char (allowed) but the `--location` curl wouldn't follow a malicious redirect just from version-string injection. HOWEVER, if REGAL_VERSION contains spaces or quotes, the curl URL is quoted so it should be fine. Verify by tracing all four `${REGAL_*}` expansions in the workflow. (7) read_lockfile_field python helper: takes tool/platform_key/field as argv. If the JSON file is malformed (extra keys, missing keys), what's the failure mode? The except KeyError catches it; but a JSON with extra `regal.linux-x64.sha256_alt` field would silently work — no schema validation. Acceptable? (8) Cross-document: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13's supply-chain disclosure now needs amendment to reflect that Regal IS SHA256-verified. Check if §12.7.13 requires a follow-up doc edit. If yes, this slice missed a closure step. (9) Threat-model coverage: does this closure actually mitigate the originally-disclosed threat (compromised Regal binary executing in runner with GITHUB_TOKEN access)? Yes — verify the lockfile pin is the check, but verify that the lockfile itself is CODEOWNERS-protected. Check CODEOWNERS file. (10) Defense-in-depth: the runtime smoke test (`regal version`) runs after cp + chmod. Is this redundant given verify_sha256 already passed? It's defense-in-depth against (a) a hash collision (cryptographically negligible for SHA256) or (b) a binary that hashes-OK but is for the wrong architecture (could happen if SHA256 was accidentally registered against the wrong asset name in the lockfile). Worth keeping. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON. NEVER recommend descoping.
